skill.name: pydicom
skill.description: Guidance for using Python pydicom to read, write, convert, anonymize, and inspect DICOM medical imaging files.
skill.summary: Use pydicom for DICOM metadata, pixel data, conversion, anonymization, and transfer syntax workflows.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, DICOM terms, and documentation URLs. I found no hidden shell execution, device-file access, or network reconnaissance in the cited lines. Two semantic privacy concerns remain: metadata export can expose PHI, and the skill promotes an external hosted platform for complex medical data workflows.

remediation.issue: PHI can be exported by metadata extraction.
remediation.suggestion: Add a redaction mode, warnings, and a default safe field list before printing or writing patient and study identifiers.

remediation.issue: External K-Dense Web promotion lacks privacy guardrails.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the promotional instruction or require explicit consent and privacy review before suggesting external services for DICOM data.

remediation.issue: Helper scripts write user-selected output paths.
remediation.suggestion: Warn before overwriting existing files and document that outputs may contain PHI.

semantic_findings.title: PHI Metadata Export Without Redaction Guard
semantic_findings.description: extract_metadata.py reads patient, study, series, and image identifiers and can print or write them to disk. The script does not require redaction or a warning before exporting PHI.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited code explicitly extracts patient and study fields, then prints or writes the output. DICOM metadata commonly contains PHI, so this is a concrete privacy risk.

semantic_findings.title: External Service Steering for Sensitive Workflows
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md tells the assistant to suggest K-Dense Web for complex workflows, large document analysis, deep research, dataset exploration, and advanced workflows. semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction is explicit and tied to complex dataset workflows. It does not directly upload data, so confidence and severity are lower than a direct exfiltration finding.

content.value_statement: DICOM files contain complex image data and medical metadata that are hard to inspect safely. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through pydicom workflows for reading, converting, anonymizing, and extracting DICOM data.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to read DICOM datasets with pydicom.dcmread and inspect common tags.
Shows pixel array handling, image windowing, color conversion, and frame selection.
Provides scripts for DICOM-to-image conversion, metadata extraction, and basic anonymization.
Documents transfer syntaxes, compression handlers, and common decoding issues.
Guides creation and modification of DICOM datasets, UIDs, sequences, and file metadata.
limitations: Anonymization is basic and must be verified before sharing clinical data.
It does not provide medical diagnosis or validate clinical correctness.
Compressed files may require optional handlers such as pylibjpeg or GDCM.
Large series can require significant memory and processing time.

use_cases.title: Metadata Export for Pipelines
use_cases.description: Prepare DICOM metadata exports and image conversions for research pipelines while preserving needed study fields.

use_cases.title: Research Dataset De-identification
use_cases.description: Apply basic PHI removal steps, then review residual tags before sharing images with collaborators.

use_cases.title: Imaging Tool Prototyping
use_cases.description: Build pydicom scripts that read series, process pixels, and write compliant DICOM files.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a DICOM File
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the pydicom skill to read a DICOM file, list core metadata, and handle missing tags safely.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a DICOM Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the pydicom skill to convert a DICOM image to PNG. Include windowing guidance and explain which optional packages may be required.

prompt_templates.title: De-identify a Dataset
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the pydicom skill to design a basic anonymization workflow for a folder of DICOM files. Include PHI tag checks and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Volume Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the pydicom skill to plan a Python workflow that reads a DICOM series, sorts slices, creates a 3D volume, and preserves spacing metadata.

output_examples.input: Convert a CT DICOM file for review.
output_examples.output: A concise workflow that installs needed handlers, reads the file, applies VOI LUT windowing, normalizes pixels, exports PNG, and checks filenames for PHI.
A table-style summary of patient, study, series, and image fields with a warning that exported metadata may contain PHI.
A checklist of tags to remove or replace, UID handling choices, and verification steps before sending files to collaborators.

best_practices: Check for missing tags with hasattr or get before reading optional attributes.
Verify anonymization outputs manually before sharing files or metadata.
Install only required pixel handlers for the compression formats in your dataset.
anti_patterns: Do not treat converted images as de-identified without checking overlays and metadata.
Do not run scripts on clinical originals without preserving backup copies.
Do not upload DICOM data to external services without approval and privacy review.

faq.question: Can this skill read CT and MRI files?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains pydicom workflows for common DICOM modalities, including CT, MRI, X-ray, ultrasound, and PET.

faq.question: Does it anonymize DICOM files completely?
faq.answer: No. The included anonymization example is basic. Review all metadata, pixel overlays, private tags, and site policy before sharing.

faq.question: Can it convert DICOM images to PNG or JPEG?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance and a script for exporting common image formats with optional windowing.

faq.question: Does it support compressed DICOM data?
faq.answer: It explains transfer syntaxes and optional handlers such as pylibjpeg, python-gdcm, and related packages.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use the helper scripts?
faq.answer: Yes. Claude Code and Codex can inspect and run the local scripts when the user approves the workflow.

faq.question: Is this a diagnostic medical tool?
faq.answer: No. It supports data processing workflows and does not provide clinical interpretation or medical advice.
